title: Deployment resilience lattice with compatibility scoring and graceful throttles
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We need a unified routing and fallback mechanism for model variant rollouts that minimizes customer-visible regressions while maximizing throughput utilization across tiers and regions. Existing heuristics rely on coarse health checks and simple percent-based canaries which don't capture subtle semantic incompatibilities between model variants, nor do they negotiate tiered capacity gracefully during bursts.

Goal: Build a 'resilience lattice' — an orchestration layer that combines compatibility scoring, topology-aware throttles, and progressive admission control to drive canaries, A/B experiments, shadowing, and auto-rollbacks. The lattice should provide deterministic routing decisions, measurable rollback triggers, and safe degraded modes that preserve latency SLOs when capacity or compatibility falls below thresholds.
rationale: Many production regressions come from semantic drift (model outputs that are syntactically valid but semantically different), uneven regional capacity, and sudden traffic spikes. By making routing decisions based on a multi-dimensional score (compatibility, latency tail, token-cost delta, region proximity) we can preferentially route sensitive traffic to safe variants and fall back to degraded but cost-lower options when needed. This reduces noisy rollbacks and churn for engineers while improving customer continuity.
success_metrics: Reduce rollback-triggered outages by 50% over next quarter
Decrease mean time to rollback detection from 6m to <90s for semantic regressions
Maintain p99 latency within existing SLOs for >95% of requests during rollouts
Limit percentage of global traffic affected by a single-region failure to <2% via topology-aware rerouting
scope: Design and implement the routing layer, compatibility scoring service, admission controller, and CLI/Console controls for rollout policies. Integrate with existing canary telemetry (evals) and Console dashboards. Implement automatic rollback hooks tied to scoring thresholds and quality alerts.
non_goals: We will not modify model training or evaluation tooling in this ticket. Deep semantic evaluation model development (e.g., new eval models) will be handled in a follow-up. This ticket also does not change billing logic or introduce new pricing tiers.
proposal:
1) Compatibility scoring microservice that consumes eval snapshots (prompt sets) and runtime signals (per-route n-gram drift, token cost delta, semantic similarity scores) to emit a per-variant compatibility score (0-100).
2) Resilience lattice router: a policy engine that combines compatibility score, region proximity, capacity tier, and latency headroom to compute route weights. Supports rules: prefer >=80 score for sensitive routes, degrade to cached prefix variant when score <60, and divert 100% traffic to fallback model if score <40.
3) Topology-aware throttles: admission controller that applies soft throttles (graceful reject with 429 hinting, or queueing) instead of hard failures when capacity limits reached; per-customer and global modes.
4) Auto-rollback orchestrator: when rolling out, monitor compatibility and latency metrics; if a scoring-policy is violated for N consecutive windows, trigger automated rollback with annotated incident and optional human confirmation for critical customers.
5) Console UI: rollout timeline, live compatibility heatmap per region, preflight simulation, and one-click abort/rollback.
6) Integrations: connect to KV cache invalidation APIs so fallback to cached prefixes preserves state where feasible.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (2 sprints): implement scoring service prototype and expose score API; basic routing policy with hard thresholds in non-production.
Phase 2 (3 sprints): build lattice router and admission controller; integrate with canary pipeline; add soft-throttle behavior.
Phase 3 (2 sprints): Console controls, automated rollback orchestrator, preflight simulation, and runbook.
Canary: start with internal-only routes, then trusted customers, then full fleet over 24-72h with progressive weights.
Fallback test matrix: region failover, tier contention, semantic-drift injection, KV cache cold-start simulation.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility service returns scores for 100% of variants used in rollouts within 200ms p50 and 1s p95
Routing layer honors policies and falls back to specified variant or cached-prefix mode when score < configured thresholds

Auto-rollback triggers when compatibility < configured threshold for 3 consecutive 1-minute windows and performs rollback in <2m (automated path) or raises alert for manual intervention (controlled path)
Console shows live compatibility heatmap and preflight simulation for any rollout with synthetic traffic option
No customer-visible errors beyond controlled 429s for throttled requests during staged tests
risks: False positives in semantic scoring could cause unnecessary rollbacks — mitigate by conservative default thresholds and human-in-the-loop confirmations for high-risk customers
Increased system complexity in router may cause new failure modes; include feature flags and kill-switches
Score compute cost and latency may add overhead — plan caching, batching, and async downstream scoring for low-priority routes
Throttling behavior may surface in billing disputes if customers see increased 429s — coordinate with CS/pricing team
implementation_notes:
- Scoring inputs: evaluation suite deltas, fingerprinting (n-gram & embedding drift), p99 latency delta, token-cost multiplier.
- Use a sliding window & EWMA to smooth transient spikes.
- Router should be implemented as a policy DSL compiled into optimized routing tables; keep hot-path minimal.
- Admission controller should expose backpressure hints to SDKs (Retry-After) and be pluggable per-customer.
- Persist rollout decisions and rollback reasons in control-plane audit logs for postmortems.
